1	# LOOM portal: interface for agents
2	
3	This page is for an agent (or the developer of one) that needs part of a
4	person's health context to do a task for them. It is the only document an
5	agent needs; it does not have to read LOOM's source.
6	
7	## What LOOM offers
8	
9	LOOM holds one person's health record and hands out **task-scoped,
10	expiring slices** of it. You say what task you are doing; LOOM decides
11	how deep you may see, which fields you get, and for how long.
12	
13	| Tier | What it contains | Field names |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| L0 | raw sensor signal | `raw_signal` |
16	| L1 | readings (here: hourly glucose, mg/dL) | `readings` |
17	| L2 | patterns and alerts derived from readings | `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` |
18	| L3 | plain-language constraints | `constraints` |
19	
20	L0 is the deepest (most revealing), L3 the shallowest. A tier includes the
21	shallower ones: an L2 grant may carry `constraints` too.
22	
23	## Access
24	
25	- Base URL and namespace are given to you by whoever runs the portal (for
26	  a test: `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and a namespace such as `demo`).
27	  Every call for one person goes to `/v1/<namespace>/...`.
28	- There is no login in v0.1. You identify yourself with `agent_id` (this
29	  agent instance) and `publisher` (the company or developer that ships
30	  it). In Nanda Town the gateway fills `agent_id` from the signed envelope;
31	  over plain HTTP both are claims.
32	- JSON in, JSON out. Errors are JSON `{"error": "..."}`; a malformed body
33	  gets HTTP 400 naming the missing fields.
34	
35	## Endpoints
36	
37	| Method and path | Use |
38	|---|---|
39	| `GET /health` | version and policy id |
40	| `POST /v1/<ns>/requests` | ask for access for a task; a grant carries data immediately |
41	| `POST /v1/<ns>/fetch` | get fresh data again under a grant you already hold |
42	| `GET /v1/<ns>/credit` | publisher → credit score (only publishers that have been seen) |
43	| `GET /v1/<ns>/log` | every decision so far, in order |
44	| `GET /v1/policy` | the built-in tasks, as JSON (same as the table below) |
45	| `GET /v1/<ns>/proposals/<proposal_id>` | status of a proposal for a task that is not built in (see below) |
46	
47	### `POST /v1/<ns>/requests`: body
48	
49	| Field | Required | Meaning |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| `request_id` | yes | unique per request; reuse it only to retry the same request |
52	| `agent_id` | yes | your agent instance |
53	| `publisher` | yes | who ships you |
54	| `category` | yes | `agent_for_user` (works for the person) or `care_provider` (clinician side) |
55	| `task` | yes | one of the task names below |
56	| `purpose` | no | free text, recorded |
57	| `tier` | yes | the deepest tier you ask for (`L0`..`L3`) |
58	| `fields` | yes | list of field names you ask for |
59	| `at` | yes | current time on the person's timeline, in days (number) |
60	
61	### Tasks (policy `loom-policy-0.2.0`)
62	
63	| `task` | `category` | Deepest tier | Fields you may ask for | Validity |
64	|---|---|-

input.command: B=http://127.0.0.1:8787; curl -s $B/health; echo; curl -s $B/v1/coldstart-2/credit; echo; curl -s -X POST $B/v1/coldstart-2/requests -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"request_id":"clinic-1-cv-001","agent_id":"clinic-1","publisher":"cambridge-clinic","category":"care_provider","task":"clinical_visit","purpose":"one-page pre-visit summary for tomorrow diabetes clinic appointment","tier":"L2","fields":["glucose_patterns","alerts","constraints"],"at":0}' | python3 -m json.tool

mkdir -p /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run2/out && cat > /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run2/out/clinic-1.md <<'EOF'
# Pre-visit summary: diabetes clinic appointment (tomorrow, day 1)

Prepared by `clinic-1` (cambridge-clinic) on day 0 from the patient's LOOM portal. Synthetic record. For clinician review; not a diagnosis or a treatment plan.

> **Patient confirmation still needed.** LOOM returned `confirmation: first_request` for this grant, so the patient should confirm before the clinic acts on this data. LOOM reports this requirement but does not collect the confirmation. Please get it at check-in.

## Glucose summary (CGM, last 14 days)

| Metric | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Mean glucose | 127 mg/dL | Estimated GMI is about 6.4% (3.31 + 0.02392 x mean). Data coverage is not reported, so treat this as a rough figure. |
| Coefficient of variation | 14.8% | Well under the 36% stability target. Glycemic variability is low. |
| Time in range | 100% | LOOM does not say what range it uses (probably 70-180 mg/dL). This implies no time below or above range. |
| Highest post-meal peak | 177 mg/dL | Just under 180. |

## Alerts

- **Post-meal spikes: 15 in 14 days** (about one a day). LOOM does not define its spike threshold. Because TIR is 100% and the highest peak is 177, these are rises after meals that stay under 180, not real hyperglycemia. No hypoglycemia alerts were reported.

## Constraints already on file (plain language)

- Limit added sugar
- Prefer low-glycemic foods

## Suggested talking points

1. Overall control looks good: mean 127, CV 14.8%, no time out of range. Reinforce what is working.
2. The roughly daily rises after meals are the main pattern. Ask which meals they follow, how big the portions are and what carbohydrates are in them, and whether the patient takes a walk after eating. Check that the current dietary constraints fit what the patient actually eats.
3. Confirm with the patient that there were no hypo symptoms, since none are recorded.
4. Fill in what LOOM does not hold (see the gaps below) from the chart or the patient.

## Not in LOOM (get these from the chart or the patient)

LOOM has no record of: diabetes type or diagnosis date, medications or insulin, lab A1c, weight or BP, other conditions, CGM wear time or data coverage, the exact range and spike thresholds, or how many hypo events there were. The portal holds 14 days of glucose only.

## What I got from LOOM and how I used it

- **Request:** task `clinical_visit`, category `care_provider` (I act for the clinic, on the clinician side). I asked for tier L2 and the fields `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` and `constraints`. That is exactly the maximum the policy allows for this task. I did not ask for anything deeper or extra.
- **Result:** `granted` (grant `g-1456dbfd25`). I got L2 and all three fields. The grant is valid for 14 days (expires on day 14) and is not single-use. Publisher credit went from 60 to 61. Friction band is medium, with `confirmation: first_request` and no auto-renew.
- **How I used it:** `glucose_patterns` gave the metrics table and the GMI estimate. `alerts` gave the post-meal spike pattern and talking point 2. `constraints` are listed as given. I made one request and no fetches. The patient-confirmation requirement is passed on at the top of this summary. I did not ask for raw readings (L1/L0). The task does not allow them, and a pre-visit summary does not need them.
EOF

input.message: I wrote the one-page pre-visit summary to /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run2/out/clinic-1.md, ending with the "What I got from LOOM and how I used it" section. I sent one request to LOOM as `clinic-1` / `cambridge-clinic`, with category `care_provider` and task `clinical_visit` at tier L2. I asked for exactly the three fields the task allows: `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` and `constraints`. It was granted in full (grant `g-1456dbfd25`, valid 14 days, credit 60 to 61), so there was no overreach and I made no fetches. The 14-day data shows a mean glucose of 127 mg/dL (my estimate is a GMI of about 6.4%), a CV of 14.8%, 100% time in range, and a highest post-meal peak of 177. It also shows 15 post-meal spike alerts, about one a day, and two diet constraints: limit added sugar and prefer low-glycemic foods. The summary turns this into suggested talking points, with the main one being the daily rises after meals. It also lists what LOOM doesn't hold for the clinic to fill in: medications, lab A1c, diabetes type, wear time, and the range and spike thresholds LOOM uses. One open item: LOOM set `confirmation: first_request`, so the patient has to confirm before the clinic acts on the data. LOOM doesn't collect that confirmation, so the note at the top of the summary asks for it at check-in.
